title: Trace dashboard access and alert delivery boundaries
description: Switch scenarios to see which Kibana, Elasticsearch, saved-object, scheduler, and connector boundary owns the outcome. A visible dashboard and a delivered notification require different chains of evidence.

nodes.label: Operator
nodes.detail: Opens a dashboard or manages a rule within one Kibana space. The user's effective access is the union of assigned roles.

nodes.label: Role + space
nodes.detail: Controls which Kibana features are visible and whether the user has read or write access in the selected space.

nodes.label: Kibana server
nodes.detail: Loads saved content, constructs Elasticsearch requests, renders results, and runs application services. It does not own the source telemetry.

nodes.label: Elasticsearch data
nodes.detail: Stores and indexes source documents, enforces index privileges, executes searches, and computes aggregations.

nodes.label: Saved objects
nodes.detail: Stores dashboards, data views, visualizations, rules, and references in Kibana-managed Elasticsearch indices.

nodes.label: Task Manager
nodes.detail: Schedules and runs Kibana background tasks, including rule checks. A delayed task can create an evaluation gap.

nodes.label: Connector
nodes.detail: Holds the integration configuration used to send an action. Deleting or disabling it does not remove the rule that references it.

nodes.label: Notification target
nodes.detail: Receives the email, webhook, ticket, or chat message after a connector action succeeds.

scenarios.label: Dashboard works
scenarios.summary: The operator has Dashboard read access in the operations space, the saved object and its references exist, and the role can read the underlying indices.
scenarios.result: Kibana can load the dashboard definition and ask Elasticsearch for the scoped data. The panels render from Elasticsearch responses.

scenarios.label: Panels forbidden
scenarios.summary: The operator can open the Kibana feature and saved dashboard, but the Elasticsearch role lacks read access to the data indices.
scenarios.result: The dashboard shell can be visible while panels fail. Kibana feature privileges do not grant access to Elasticsearch documents.

scenarios.label: Broken saved object
scenarios.summary: A dashboard was promoted without a referenced data view or visualization, even though the production indices are healthy.
scenarios.result: The content is incomplete. Export and import the reference graph rather than treating one dashboard record as a standalone file.

scenarios.label: Alert delivered
scenarios.summary: Task Manager runs the scheduled rule, Elasticsearch returns matching evidence, and the configured connector action succeeds.
scenarios.result: The rule check creates or updates alert state, then the action sends a notification. Detection and delivery are separate outcomes.

scenarios.label: Rule runs late
scenarios.summary: Task Manager is delayed. The data still exists in Elasticsearch, but the scheduled check did not run at its intended time.
scenarios.result: Treat the interval as an evaluation gap. A quiet notification channel is not proof that the monitored condition stayed healthy.

scenarios.label: Action fails
scenarios.summary: The rule evaluates its condition, but the referenced connector was deleted or is unavailable.
scenarios.result: Kibana can still create alert state, but the action fails and no external notification is delivered. Monitor rule and connector execution separately.
